![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/d4bcdb6515b262c070c7ed689263efbbde8a350ad6a28b4fc106de281e69ff46.png)

Find the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2t,\,y=t\operatorname{sin}⁡t
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [0,\pi ].$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot 2\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a positive number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\ge 0$ for all $t\in [0,\pi ].$

To solve the above integral, we use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡t & ⇒ & v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =2t(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)(1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-2(\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -0\operatorname{cos}⁡0)+2(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =-2\pi (-1) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
